$comment: The catch-all rewrite is what makes client-side routing work: /invoices/34 has no
file behind it, so it must return index.html for the router to resolve.
/assets/ is excluded deliberately. Vercel serves an existing file before any rewrite,
so this changes nothing for assets that are present — but a MISSING one was falling
through to the rewrite and being answered with index.html at 200. The browser then
received HTML where it had asked for a module, which surfaces as the useless
'Failed to fetch dynamically imported module' rather than an honest 404.
That happens after every deploy: hashed filenames change, the old files are removed,
and any tab still running the previous build asks for chunks that no longer exist.
With this exclusion the request 404s, which is both diagnosable and something the
app can detect and recover from — see lazyImport in src/utils/lazyImport.js.
